speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning. To help me understand your chronic cough, could you describe the nature of the sputum you produce and how long this condition has been bothering you?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old woman. The patient has been experiencing an aggressive cough producing copious amounts of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum for about 11 years, with exacerbations similar to the current presentation today. Reports that the cough is worse in the morning and has had multiple evaluations in the past due to recurrent bouts of bronchitis requiring antibiotics treatment. The patient is a non-smoker.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience shortness of breath or wheezing during these episodes, and has there been any history of recurrent sinus infections or nasal polyps? I would also like to know if you have any known allergies or asthma.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Aggressive cough with thick, yellow-green sputum. I also have Cough worse in the morning, History of recurrent bronchitis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a history of recurrent sinus infections, nasal polyps, or asthma, and does your family have any history of cystic fibrosis? I would also like to check for clubbing of your fingers and signs of bronchiectasis on examination. REQUEST TEST: High-Resolution CT Chest

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the CT scan is normal, I need to rule out other causes of chronic productive cough. Do you experience heartburn, regurgitation, or a sour taste in your mouth, particularly after meals or when lying down?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No other significant past medical history aside from the recurrent bronchitis. Social history: Non-smoker, no history of alcohol or drug abuse.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal CT and lack of sinus history, I need to rule out airway hyperreactivity. Do you experience wheezing, chest tightness, or shortness of breath that worsens at night or with exercise? REQUEST TEST: Spirometry_with_Bronchodilator

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: FVC: Reduced, FEV1: Reduced, FEV1/FVC Ratio: Normal

speaker: Doctor
text: The spirometry shows a restrictive pattern with a normal ratio, which is unusual for typical COPD or asthma. To further investigate the cause of your chronic productive cough, do you experience heartburn, regurgitation, or a sour taste in your mouth, particularly after meals or when lying down? REQUEST TEST: Barium_Swallow

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal imaging and swallow study, I need to consider non-anatomical causes of chronic cough. Do you experience heartburn, regurgitation, or a sour taste in your mouth, particularly after meals or when lying down? REQUEST TEST: 24hr_pH_monitoring

speaker: Doctor
text: Since GERD and structural lung diseases have been ruled out, I need to investigate other causes of chronic cough. Do you take any medications, particularly ACE inhibitors for blood pressure, or do you have a history of allergies or post-nasal drip? REQUEST TEST: Nasal_Endoscopy

speaker: Doctor
text: With structural, allergic, and GERD causes ruled out, I must consider primary ciliary dyskinesia despite the normal CT. Do you have a history of chronic otitis media, infertility, or situs inversus, and does your family have any history of recurrent respiratory infections? REQUEST TEST: Nasal_Nitric_Oxide

speaker: Doctor
text: With structural, allergic, GERD, and ciliary dyskinesia causes ruled out, and given the normal CT and spirometry, the clinical picture of chronic productive cough with purulent sputum in a non-smoker is most consistent with diffuse panbronchiolitis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Diffuse Panbronchiolitis
